tests.summary: [EC-18] AC-1, AC-2 — Carousel renders at the bottom of the Products panel on desktop
tests.precondition: Brand data source publishes 12 valid brands. Test page with an authored Products megamenu is previewed.

steps.action: Open the test page at a desktop viewport and open the Products megamenu.
steps.result: The megamenu panel opens and a brand carousel strip is rendered below all product category columns, spanning the full panel width.

steps.action: Count the circular brand logo items visible in the strip without scrolling.
steps.result: Between 5 and 7 logo items are visible simultaneously.

tests.summary: [EC-18] AC-11, AC-22 — Previous-brands arrow is disabled at the start of the track
tests.precondition: Products megamenu open at 1440x900 with 12 brands authored; carousel track at its leftmost position.

steps.result: The button carries aria-disabled="true", is styled as disabled, and remains present in the tab order.

steps.action: Move focus to the previous-brands arrow and activate it.
steps.data: Tab to the button, then press Enter, then press Space
steps.result: The carousel track does not scroll and its scroll offset is unchanged.

tests.summary: [EC-18] AC-10 — Next-brands arrow advances the track by one item width
tests.precondition: Products megamenu open at 1440x900 with 12 brands authored; track at its leftmost position.

steps.action: Note the first fully visible brand, then click the next-brands arrow once.
steps.result: The track scrolls forward by one logo width and the previously second brand is now first in the visible window.
The track scrolls back by the same amount and returns to its original position.

tests.summary: [EC-18] AC-6 — Carousel zone is absent from the DOM when the brand list is empty
tests.precondition: Brand data source publishes zero rows.

steps.action: Open the Products megamenu at 1440x900 and inspect the panel markup.
steps.result: No carousel container, strip, heading, or arrow button exists in the DOM — not merely hidden with CSS.

steps.action: Inspect the panel layout and the browser console.
steps.result: Product category columns fill the panel with no empty gap where the carousel would sit, and no uncaught error is logged.

tests.summary: [EC-18] AC-6 — Carousel is suppressed when the brand data source fetch fails
tests.precondition: Brand data source request is forced to fail (block the request or return HTTP 500).

steps.action: Open the Products megamenu at 1440x900 with the data request failing.
steps.result: The carousel zone is absent from the DOM and the megamenu remains fully usable.
A warning is logged for the failed fetch and no uncaught exception is thrown.

tests.summary: [EC-18] AC-5, AC-16 — Mobile renders a touch-scrollable strip with no arrow buttons
tests.precondition: 12 brands authored. Mobile drawer navigation available.

steps.action: Load the test page at a mobile viewport, open the navigation drawer, and enter the Products section.
steps.result: A horizontal strip of circular brand logos is rendered inline in the Products drawer section.

steps.action: Inspect the strip for arrow controls.
steps.result: No previous or next arrow button exists anywhere in the strip markup.

steps.action: Swipe the strip horizontally, then scroll the drawer vertically.
steps.result: The strip scrolls horizontally with momentum and the drawer still scrolls vertically without interference.

tests.summary: [EC-18] AC-21 — Each brand logo link exposes the authored brand name as its accessible name
tests.precondition: 12 brands authored, each with a brand name, logo and destination URL.

steps.action: Open the Products megamenu at 1440x900 and inspect the accessibility tree for the carousel region.
steps.result: Every logo is exposed as a link whose accessible name equals its authored brand name; none is empty or generic.

tests.summary: [EC-18] AC-12 — Tapping a brand logo on mobile closes the drawer and navigates to the brand page
tests.precondition: 12 brands authored with valid destination URLs. Mobile drawer open on the Products section.

steps.action: Tap the first brand logo in the strip.
steps.result: The navigation drawer closes and the browser navigates to that brand's authored destination URL.

steps.action: Confirm the destination page has loaded.
steps.result: The brand page renders and no drawer overlay remains on screen.
